questions: Is the tremor present when your hands are completely relaxed in your lap?
Is there a family history of similar tremors?
Does drinking alcohol temporarily reduce the tremor?
Do you have trouble sleeping or notice your leg moving restlessly at night?
At what age did you first notice this tremor?
Has the tremor been getting gradually worse over time?
Are you taking any medications, including over-the-counter drugs or supplements?
Do you consume a lot of caffeine, such as coffee or energy drinks?
Does the tremor also affect your head or voice?
Is the tremor worse in one hand than the other?
Does the tremor occur during other tasks like eating, drinking, or writing?
Does anyone else in your extended family have a similar tremor (parents, grandparents, aunts, uncles)?
Does the tremor get worse when you feel anxious or stressed?
Do you notice any stiffness in your arms or legs?
Has anyone commented that you've been moving slower than usual?
Do you notice any tremor in your legs when sitting?
Has anyone noticed any abnormal posturing of your neck or wrist?
Do you notice the tremor more when you're trying to hold something still versus when you're actively moving?
Do you feel anxious or have you noticed any mood changes recently?
Can you write a sentence for me to examine?
Does the tremor stop completely when you rest your hands in your lap?
Does the tremor get worse with fatigue or at the end of the day?
Have you tried beta-blockers like propranolol, or has anyone prescribed them for you?
Do you notice any cramping or pain in your forearm when the tremor is active?
Have you tried holding a glass of water with your arm outstretched to see if it trembles?
When you pour from a pitcher or use a screwdriver, does the tremor get worse?
Has your handwriting become messier or more shaky over the years?
Has any doctor ever suggested this might be essential tremor?
orders: Neurological examination for cerebellar signs (finger-to-nose, heel-to-shin, dysdiadochokinesia)
Blood tests: TSH, free T4, ceruloplasmin, serum copper, liver function tests
Spiral drawing test (to assess tremor pattern and amplitude)
Assessment of tremor frequency using smartphone accelerometry or clinical observation
Evaluation for wing-beating tremor (arms abducted and flexed)
DaT-SPECT (dopamine transporter scan) to evaluate for early parkinsonism
Detailed neurological examination of hand tremor characteristics: tremor frequency estimate by clinical observation or tuning fork comparison
Entrainment test: tapping rhythmically with the non-trembling hand to see if tremor frequency changes
Distractibility test: performing a mental task (serial 7s) or Contralateral limb movement while observing tremor
Assessment of tremor variability: prolonged observation (2-3 minutes) noting consistency of amplitude and frequency
